title: Where You Are on the Map
summary: Automator = virtual worker — Time Audit before using any tool

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Before building any automation, you need to know which repetitive tasks take up your time each week.
- Why now? After Builder (the product) and Creator (the audience), Automator is the «virtual worker» that makes repetitive tasks run on their own.
- What after the lesson? You will identify 5 repetitive tasks and calculate the time you waste on them weekly.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You hear about Make, Zapier, and n8n — you open YouTube and build a Flow — and after a week, you are still doing the same work manually.
- The problem is not the tool. The problem is you did not identify which tasks are repetitive and actually waste your time.
- The virtual worker does not appear out of nowhere — it works on clear and repetitive tasks that you identified first.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: Identify Wasted Time, Then Hand Over to the Virtual Worker
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Automator = building a «virtual worker» that repeats your repetitive tasks: responses, data transfer, reminders, follow-ups.
- Builder created the product. Creator brought the people. Automator connects the two and saves hours each week.
- The first step is not a tool — it is a Time Audit: which task do you do more than twice a week? How many minutes each time?
- When you identify the 5 most repetitive tasks, you will know where the virtual worker should start.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Building Tools vs. Knowing Where Time Goes
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Building Without Audit | Audit First |
|-------------------|-------------|
| Opening Make and building 3 Flows — but still sending welcome emails manually for an hour daily — automation is not about the task that wastes time | Count: Welcome email × 20 clients × 3 minutes = 1 hour daily. First Flow = automatic welcome email. Save 5 hours weekly |

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: Sarah sends a welcome email to each new client manually — 30 minutes daily. What is the best step before opening any automation tool?
Count the task, its time, and frequency per week — to know this is a priority.
Explanation: Audit first — when you know «welcome email» = 30 minutes daily, you will know this is the first task for the virtual worker.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Conduct a Time Audit for Your Week
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Monitoring — not building. Before handing over any work to the virtual worker, you need to know the repetitive tasks. 10–15 minutes is enough. Submission: 5 tasks (name · times/week · minutes/time · total) · biggest time waster · simplest task · first automation + reason Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 5 Tasks with Numbers | 60% | Each task includes times and minutes; the total weekly is calculated |
| Priority Decision | 40% | Biggest time waster + simplest task; the choice of the first automation has a reason |
